_README: CURATED CONFIG -- intended for domain-expert review, deliberately kept out of code.
Channel D (outcome annotation) uses this to answer 'so what?' after Channel A finds a
pharmacokinetic effect. Channel A can say 'Simvastatin's clearance is inhibited, so its
exposure rises' -- true but incomplete, because it never says why rising simvastatin
exposure matters. This maps a DrugBank category on the AFFECTED drug to the plain-English
consequence of having more of that drug in the body.
Combined, the two produce the full statement: 'exposure to Simvastatin rises -- a drug
flagged as causing muscle toxicity (myopathy / rhabdomyolysis)'.
DIFFERENT FROM risk_axes.json, which some categories also appear in: an AXIS fires when
2+ drugs SHARE it (additive effect between drugs). An OUTCOME CLASS fires for a SINGLE
drug whose exposure is being raised by something else (consequence of accumulation).
Same category can legitimately serve both roles.
Phrasing must describe the consequence of MORE of the drug, and stay factual -- this text
is shown to the user as a direct statement, so it must not overclaim severity.
